name: Understanding cause and effect
gist: Papers studying causal relationships in data—what causes what, how to infer hidden causes, and how to design experiments and systems that account for causality.
explain: Correlation is not causation — this is the oldest lesson in statistics, yet it is still the hardest to apply. If you notice that ice cream sales are high when swimming pool drownings are high, correlation is real, but neither causes the other — both happen because it is summer. Yet if you see that people who take a drug get healthier, you need to know: does the drug make them healthier, or are healthier people more likely to seek out that drug? In a real-world system, you observe correlations everywhere, but the causal relationships are hidden. You need to figure out which variables actually influence which others, and how much.

The challenge is that in most real data, you cannot run experiments. You see what happened, but you do not see what would have happened if you changed one thing. If a student scores well on a test, you see that fact, but you never see what score the same student would have gotten if they had studied a different amount. To infer causation from pure observation, you need clever reasoning and assumptions about the underlying structure of how the world works — for example, assuming that grades depend on study time, that study time depends on motivation, and that motivation is not directly affected by test scores.

Researchers use graphical models to map out cause-and-effect relationships, identify which relationships they can and cannot infer from data, and design experiments or observations that reveal causation. Some use causal diagrams that show which variables influence which, then use data to estimate the strength of those influences. Some use techniques from do-calculus, a formal system for reasoning about what would happen if you forced a particular action (for example, if you forced someone to study more). The goal is to distinguish what-if questions (if we change X, does Y change?) from mere correlation.

papers.title: Causal Discovery for Irregularly Time Series with Consistency Guarantees
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical consistency guarantees for structure recovery and outperforms existing methods under irregular sampling and high missingness.

papers.title: Causal Discovery via Quantile Partial Effect
papers.contribution: Achieves identifiability without requiring mechanisms or Markov assumptions, effectively distinguishes causal directions through basis function tests on large bivariate datasets.

papers.title: Characterization and Learning of Causal Graphs with Latent Confounders and Post-treatment Selection from Interventional Data
papers.contribution: The framework characterizes Markov properties and enables identification of causal relations, latent confounders, and post-treatment selection patterns.

papers.title: Is Your LLM Overcharging You? Tokenization, Transparency, and Incentives
papers.contribution: Token-based pricing mechanisms are vulnerable to strategic misreporting; character-based pricing eliminates the financial incentive while allowing providers to maintain average margins.

papers.title: On Measuring Influence in Avoiding Undesired Future
papers.contribution: Reveals counterintuitive insight that influential variables may not have intrinsically strong causal effects; demonstrates utility of altering weak causal factors or non-intrinsic variables.

papers.title: ALM-MTA: Front-Door Causal Multi-Touch Attribution Method for Creator-Ecosystem Optimization
papers.contribution: On 400 million DAU platform: increased DAU with 0.04%, improved upload AUC by 40%, and increased unit exposure efficiency by 670% over SOTA.

papers.title: Causal Structure Learning in Hawkes Processes with Complex Latent Confounder Networks
papers.contribution: The method effectively recovers causal structures despite latent subprocesses, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for identifiability.

papers.title: Direct Doubly Robust Estimation of Conditional Quantile Contrasts
papers.contribution: The method outperforms existing procedures in estimation accuracy across multiple data scenarios while improving interpretability.

papers.title: Embracing Discrete Search: A Reasonable Approach to Causal Structure Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves highly accurate structure recovery with near-perfect reconstruction in standard settings and substantially reduced runtime.

papers.title: Enhancing Affine Maximizer Auctions with Correlation-Aware Payment
papers.contribution: Shows scenarios where classic AMAs perform arbitrarily poorly while CA-AMA reaches optimal revenue, with practical algorithm achieving improved revenue across various distributions.

papers.title: Feasible Fusion: Constrained Joint Estimation under Structural Non-Overlap
papers.contribution: Achieves gains over baselines on large-scale ride-hailing, matching models with significantly more RCT data.

papers.title: Matching without Group Barrier for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation
papers.contribution: Improved counterfactual prediction in both binary and multiple treatment settings through cross-group neighbor selection.

papers.title: Model Fusion via Retrofitting
papers.contribution: Consistent improvements over baselines on VGGs, ResNets, ViTs with largest gains in zero-shot and non-IID scenarios.

papers.title: Modeling Covariate Transition for Efficient Estimation of Longitudinal Treatment Effects in Randomized Experiments
papers.contribution: Enables more powerful statistical inference on longitudinal treatment effects with practical advantages demonstrated on A/B test data.

papers.title: Modeling Interference for Treatment Effect Estimation in Network Dynamic Environment
papers.contribution: DSPNET demonstrates superiority over state-of-the-art approaches for treatment effect estimation in dynamic network environments with interference.

papers.title: Off-Policy Evaluation with Strategic Agents via Local Disclosure
papers.contribution: Enables OPE in one-shot settings with partial knowledge of agent response behavior; establishes consistency of proposed estimator.

papers.title: On the Coordination of Value-Maximizing Bidders
papers.contribution: Show coordination improves both Return-on-Spend compliance and total value accrued for participating auto-bidders across broad algorithm classes.

papers.title: Once-More: Continuous Self-Correction for Large Language Models via Perplexity-Guided Intervention
papers.contribution: Once-More achieves state-of-the-art self-correction results, first post-hoc method to leverage token perplexity and external feedback for continuous correction.

papers.title: Risk-Averse and Optimistic Advertiser Incentive Compatibility in Auto-bidding
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that the Second-Price Auction satisfies both RAIC and OAIC, clarifying its incentive properties under auto-bidding with constraint multiplicity.

papers.title: Score-based Greedy Search for Structure Identification of Partially Observed Linear Causal Models
papers.contribution: Enables identification of structure including latent variables up to Markov equivalence class with well-defined operators for efficient graph space search.

papers.title: Selling Data as a Digital Good with Scaling Valuations
papers.contribution: Characterizes profit-optimal mechanisms and shows simple two-stage algorithm achieves constant-factor approximation to offline optimum under demand uncertainty.

papers.title: The (Marginal) Value of a Search Ad: An Online Causal Framework for Repeated Second-price Auctions
papers.contribution: Attains rate-optimal regret under several feedback models with improvement over first-price auction settings.

papers.title: The Fairness Hierarchy: A viewpoint from causal inference
papers.contribution: Our empirical experiments demonstrate how different fairness levels can be instantiated and compared in practice
